title: Set Matrix Zeroes
summary: Given an m x n integer matrix, if an element is zero, set its entire row and column to zeros.
statement: Given an m x n integer matrix, if an element is zero, set its entire row and column to zeros. Perform this operation in place.
constraints: 1–200 rows and columns; values are signed 32-bit integers.
Every zero in the original matrix clears its entire row and column. Newly written zeros must not trigger additional clearing. Modify matrix in place; target constant extra space.
hints: Remember which rows and columns originally contained zeros before clearing other cells.
Store row and column flags in the matrix's first column and row, with separate booleans for those two borders.
Record the two border flags, mark interior zeros, clear interiors using either marker, then clear flagged borders last.
Processing border markers too early destroys the distinction between original zeros and generated zeros.
editorial: Use the first row and column as marker storage for the remaining matrix. Record whether each border initially needs clearing, because their shared corner cannot encode both facts. Scan the interior to mark affected rows/columns, clear marked interior cells, and only then clear the two borders according to their saved flags. The oracle instead lists original zero coordinates and builds each output cell from that immutable snapshot.

tests.explanation: Only the center's original row and column clear, leaving the four corners equal to 1.
The first row clears along with columns 0 and 3. The other rows retain their middle entries.
